clue.text: Sullen expression of annoyance in Commons

indicators.note: in tells us the cry of annoyance sits inside the word for commons

parts.note: commons are rations or food provided, i.e. fare
ouch is what you say when hurt or annoyed

explanation.surface: Someone sulkily mutters a complaint in the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commons' looks like Parliament, but here it is the old sense of food shared at a common table, as in a college.
explanation.definitionFit: Farouche is a French borrowing for shy, unsociable or sullen in manner.

clue.text: Judge turns extremely catty about archdeacon's intensity of belief

indicators.note: about means the judge-and-catty letters go around the archdeacon
turns tells us the judge's word is read backwards

parts.note: a ref, referee, judges a match

indicators.note: extremely means take the first and last letters of catty

parts.note: Ven, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A judge grows bitchy towards a senior cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses the judge's word; 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of catty; these two pieces go 'about' the archdeacon's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervency is passionate ardour, the warmth of deeply held conviction.

clue.text: Logical basis for action Malvolio would approve of?

parts.note: the puritanical steward in Twelfth Night disapproves of revelry, so would favour restricting beer
the puritanical steward in Twelfth Night disapproves of revelry, so would favour restricting beer

explanation.surface: A reason for doing something that Shakespeare's killjoy steward would endorse.
explanation.walkthrough: In Twelfth Night Sir Toby taunts the puritanical steward about 'cakes and ale'; split the answer into two words to find what such a killjoy would want.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning or justification behind a course of action.

clue.text: Amulet, no end variegated, used by Moslem doctors

indicators.note: variegated means patterned in varied colours, so the letters are mixed up
no end means amulet loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A multicoloured charm, chipped at one end, is worn by Islamic physicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' cuts AMULET to AMULE, and 'variegated' rearranges those letters. 'doctors' means learned scholars, not physicians.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulema are the body of Muslim scholars learned in religious law, doctors in the academic sense.

clue.text: Young Henry has one objection To fish

parts.note: Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare
I is the Roman numeral one
but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: A young prince has a single complaint about eating fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The halibut is a large flatfish of northern seas.

clue.text: To be consistent. Hero in Much Ado is seen in church

indicators.note: is seen in tells us the jumbled hero letters appear inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: being in much ado means in a fuss or commotion, so the letters of hero are thrown about

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Hero, from Much Ado About Nothing, is spotted at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Hero really is a character in Much Ado About Nothing, which disguises 'in Much Ado' (in a commotion) as the anagram signal; 'is seen in' marks the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hold together logically, to be consistent.

clue.text: Nymphs from a seaside resort

indicators.note: from signals that the nymphs are made out of the resort's letters

parts.note: Oceanside is a seaside town in California

explanation.surface: Sea nymphs hail from a beach town.
explanation.walkthrough: The resort is not printed: think of OCEANSIDE and rearrange its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oceanids were the sea nymphs, daughters of Oceanus in Greek myth.

clue.text: Mrs Dombey sounds tied up with husband

indicators.note: up here means disturbed, so the letters of tied are mixed

explanation.surface: Mrs Dombey seems tied down by her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' marks the anagram of tied; 'sounds' just links, as in 'sounds like'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Granger becomes the second wife of Mr Dombey in Dickens's Dombey and Son.

clue.text: Prize for the best battery?

parts.note: battery hens lay eggs, so a trophy for their best laying would be a little holder for a boiled one

explanation.surface: An award for the top power cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cup holding a boiled egg at table is jokingly the trophy for battery hens.

clue.text: Concentrate on providing a complete range

parts.note: to mass is to gather or concentrate
if means providing, on condition that

explanation.surface: Focus on offering the full spectrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places the condition word after the concentrate word; 'range' means mountains, not a full spectrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact mountain group forming a single block of high ground.

clue.text: Blooming early, and quite unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for quite loses its final letter

parts.note: rather means quite, as in rather good

explanation.surface: Something flowers early and only partly done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the last R from RATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Rathe is an old poetic adjective for early, used of flowers that bloom before the season.

clue.text: Modifying directions in a legacy

indicators.note: in places the two compass directions inside the word for a legacy

parts.note: a leaving is something left behind, a legacy
E and N are east and north, compass directions

explanation.surface: Instructions in a will are being amended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'directions' looks like instructions in the will, but is just E and N, put 'in' LEAVING, an old word for what someone leaves you.
explanation.definitionFit: Leavening is a transforming influence that alters the whole, like yeast in dough.

clue.text: Sort of bun bears love makes a friend for Antony

indicators.note: sort of signals a version or rearrangement of the letters that follow

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A kind of bun the bears adore wins over a man called Antony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges BUN, BEARS and O together.
explanation.definitionFit: Enobarbus is Mark Antony's loyal follower in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra.

clue.text: Indian governor sent back in run out

indicators.note: in puts the reversed governor inside the rearranged run
out means the letters of run are put out of order
sent back means the governor's letters are read backwards

parts.note: HE is His Excellency, the title of a colonial governor

explanation.surface: An Indian administrator is recalled after a cricketer is run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' marks the anagram of run, 'sent back' the reversal, and 'in' the container; a governor is His Excellency.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first prime minister, an Indian statesman.

clue.text: Man with another service to take uses prayer beads

parts.note: a chap is a man
in tennis a let is a serve that must be played again

explanation.surface: A man with another church service to attend uses his rosary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests church, but it is the tennis serve: a LET is replayed.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a string of beads used for counting prayers, a short rosary.

clue.text: He interrupts member, a Conservative — a Lord's idea?

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

indicators.note: interrupts means the pronoun breaks into the run of other letters

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the British Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A man cuts in on a Tory MP's speech, perhaps a peer's thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground, not a peer; the pronoun 'interrupts' the party name after the limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg theory was the cricket bowling tactic aimed at the batsman's body, notorious in the 1932-33 Bodyline series.

clue.text: The iron maiden in Sardou's play

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Dora is a girl's name, standing for a maiden

explanation.surface: The iron maiden, a torture device, appears in a French play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The iron maiden' reads as the torture device, but splits into a chemical symbol and a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Fedora is an 1882 drama by the French playwright Victorien Sardou, which gave its name to the hat.

clue.text: It's said to destroy kind of weed in the quad, for example

indicators.note: it's said signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken

parts.note: wreck means destroy, and tangle is a kind of seaweed

explanation.surface: Someone talks of ripping out weeds in the college courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weed' is seaweed: TANGLE is a type of kelp.
explanation.definitionFit: A college quadrangle is typically a four-sided courtyard with right-angled corners.

clue.text: Endymion not written in Latin but sung in Scotland

definitions.meaning: the botanical name Endymion non-scripta, Latin for 'not written', is an old name for the woodland flower
the traditional song The ... of Scotland

explanation.surface: Keats's Endymion is left untranslated into Latin but is sung north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: Endymion suggests Keats's poem, but it is the plant's old genus name.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodland wild hyacinth was once classed as Endymion non-scripta, and The Blue Bells of Scotland is a Scottish folk song.

clue.text: Cut wood and got laid off

definitions.meaning: trimmed a row of bushes, as a gardener does
in betting, to lay off is to make an opposite bet to limit loss

explanation.surface: A woodcutter finishes the job and loses employment.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedged means both trimmed a hedge and protected a wager by covering it with a counter-bet.

clue.text: This Blue is on the board

definitions.text: This Blue is on the board

parts.words: This Blue is on the board
parts.note: a blue-veined cheese from Denmark served on a cheeseboard

explanation.surface: A sportsman with a university Blue sits on a company board.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is an Oxbridge sporting award; here it is the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish Blue is a well-known blue-veined cheese, the board being a cheeseboard.

clue.text: The sort of chairs children never have enough of

definitions.text: The sort of chairs children never have enough of

parts.words: The sort of chairs children never have enough of
parts.note: a party game in which there is always one seat too few, so a child is left standing each round

explanation.surface: Children always want more seats than there are.
explanation.definitionFit: In the party game, players circle chairs while music plays, and one chair fewer than players is set out.

clue.text: Format is sensitive part for the Fauvist

indicators.note: part means the letters form part of the run of words

explanation.surface: Layout is a delicate matter for a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' marks the name sitting inside 'forMAT IS SEnsitive'.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse led the Fauves, painters known for wild bold colour.

clue.text: Tree featured in ballads by sailor about love

indicators.note: by means the ballads word stands beside the other pieces
about here means turned round, so the sailor is read backwards

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
W. S. Gilbert wrote the comic verses known as the Bab Ballads

explanation.surface: A tree crops up in songs about a lovelorn sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns AB to BA; then O; then BAB, from Gilbert's Bab Ballads.
explanation.definitionFit: The baobab is an African tree with a hugely swollen trunk.

clue.text: Character dropped by Eliza

parts.note: Eliza Doolittle in Pygmalion speaks Cockney, London working-class dialect, and omits the H sound at the start of words

explanation.surface: Eliza abandons a role in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' looks like a role or person, but it is a letter of the alphabet, named in full.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the letter H is spelt out, and Cockney speakers like Shaw's flower girl drop it from words such as 'ello.

clue.text: French recognition for British heavyweight on points

parts.note: a ton is the British unit of weight
N and E are compass points

explanation.surface: A French honour goes to a British heavyweight boxer winning on points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the compass points after the weight. The definition reads 'French recognition (for the British weight)': the metric unit uses the French spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The metric unit of a thousand kilograms takes its French spelling, the French counterpart of the British weight.

clue.text: Our mother church abroad .

parts.note: the French for Our Lady names the famous Paris cathedral

explanation.surface: The mother church of a congregation stands overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris cathedral's French name means Our Lady, the Virgin Mary, mother of Christ.

clue.text: Digs out hundreds of little creatures

indicators.note: out means the hundreds letter is taken away

parts.note: delves means digs
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Excavations turn up hundreds of tiny beings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes D from DELVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are small mischievous sprites of folklore.

clue.text: Jibs at son forming instrumental group

indicators.note: forming signals that the letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: A son balks at joining a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jibs at' looks like the verb 'balks at', but JIBS, AT and SON are simply rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Players of the banjo together make up a group of instrumentalists.

clue.text: Specific against fever? By no means

definitions.text: Specific against fever? By no means

parts.note: v stands for versus, against
ague is a malarial fever with shivering fits

explanation.surface: Is there a specific remedy for fever? Not at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Specific' is an old word for a remedy targeting one disease; V AGUE reads as against fever, and the whole clue says the result is by no means specific.
explanation.definitionFit: Vague is the opposite of precise or definite.

clue.text: Have an extra double — cheerio!

indicators.note: double means the word for an extra appears twice over

parts.note: in cricket a bye is a run scored without the batsman hitting the ball, one of the extras

explanation.surface: Someone orders another double drink and then says goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' sounds like a drink, but it repeats BYE, a cricket extra.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal farewells said on parting.

clue.text: Dance on points in contemporary programme

indicators.note: on means the dance word follows the compass points in an across entry

parts.note: N, E, W and S are the four points of the compass
a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: A ballerina dances en pointe in a modern show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on points' suggests ballet, but the points are the compass's N, E, W, S, with REEL placed after them.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsreel was a short film of current events shown in cinemas.
